key_insight: The paper introduces the first synchronized multi-view benchmark for real-world splashing liquids, enabling research on a visual phenomenon that was previously too fast, textureless, and view-dependent to reconstruct reliably. It shows that capturing splash dynamics in real scenes is now feasible and measurable.
problem_solved: Existing liquid reconstruction datasets and methods mostly handle synthetic fluids, smoke, or slow deformations, but not real splashes. This paper addresses the lack of a benchmark for reconstructing highly dynamic, short-lived splashing liquids from synchronized multi-view video.
method: Collects a benchmark of 20 real splash scenes ranging from coherent streams to violent splashes.
Uses seven synchronized cameras to capture the same event from multiple viewpoints.
Provides a challenging evaluation setting for reconstructing transient liquid shapes and motion in real-world conditions.
impact: This benchmark gives AI/ML researchers a realistic testbed for advancing multi-view reconstruction, fluid modeling, and dynamic scene understanding. Practitioners can use it to evaluate whether their methods generalize beyond synthetic or simplified liquid scenarios.

paper_title: SplashSplat: Reconstructing Splashing Liquids from Real-World Multi-View Videos
paper_authors: Peiyu Liu, Dingxi Zhang, Federico Tombari, Marc Pollefeys, Christina Tsalicoglou
